coordinates.note: The coordinate is the OpenStreetMap/Nominatim point for CERN's whole Prévessin site, not a surveyed position of the EHN1 building (Building 887, about 330 m long), so it is recorded as a campus point and shown as approximate. The site is the placement of ProtoDUNE-SP, ProtoDUNE-DP and the ICARUS refurbishment. CERN's Neutrino Platform page, the North Area pages and open-days material (checked 2026-09-17) identify the building and its general siting on the Prévessin site but give no latitude and longitude for it; treat every placement here as campus-precision.
coordinates.quote: located in a test-beam hall on CERN’s Prévessin site

name: CERN Neutrino Platform, EHN1 (Prévessin site)
notes: Coordinates are shown at campus (Prévessin-site) precision; see the coordinate note. The marker is not a claim of survey-grade precision for the EHN1 building.

summary.plain: A large hall at CERN, on the French side of the laboratory, where full-size prototypes of the DUNE detectors were built and tested in a particle beam.
summary.technical: EHN1 extension in the CERN North Area on the Prévessin site, housing the CERN Neutrino Platform test beams and the ProtoDUNE single-phase and dual-phase cryostats, as well as ICARUS refurbishment and Baby MIND.
